#Text=Once upon a time the birds took it into their heads that they would like a master , and that one of their number must be chosen king .
#Text=A meeting of all the birds was called and though they understood the birds who were from the most distant lands would be unable to come , many birds came from faraway meadows and woods .
#Text=The eagle , who already thought himself the de facto king , arrived fashionably late .
#Text=It was a hawk who was most excited about the meeting , because he was the dark horse for king .
#Text=The small fry came too , and the robin , the bluebird , the owl , the lark , and the sparrow , who had only a chance in a million to be king , were all present at the meeting .
#Text=The cuckoo , who was almost not invited because his call so annoyed the other birds , came too .
#Text=It was the very little bird who had no name at all , however , that would end up overturning the balance of power among the birds .
#Text=That there would be great confusion and noise among the birds at the meeting was to be expected , given the sheer numbers of birds that have gathered .
#Text=There was piping , hissing , and clacking , but finally it was decided that the bird that could fly the highest should be king .
#Text=The little bird lay low near the eagle at first , but the eagle did not notice the bird hopping onto his back right as the competition was about to commence .
#Text=Into the air in a great flock all the birds flew when the signal was given .
#Text=The air was full of dust , and it seemed as if a black cloud were floating over the field .
#Text=You could hear the birds chirping and flapping from fields that were miles away .
#Text=The little birds that soon grew tired fell back quickly to earth .
#Text=The fact that the larger ones held out longer , and flew higher and higher , but the eagle flew highest of any , surprised no one .
#Text=Could anyone stop the eagle that seemed to be flying straight into the sun ?
#Text=The other birds gave out one by one and when the eagle saw this he thought , `` What is the use of flying any higher ?
#Text=This victory is in the bag and I am king ! ''
#Text=Then the birds below called with one accord , `` Come back , come back !
#Text=It is you who must be our king because no one can fly as high as you . ''
#Text=`` Except me ! ''
#Text=cried a shrill , shrill voice , and out of the blue the little bird without a name rose from the eagle 's back , where he had lain hidden in the feathers .
#Text=His guile was the ace up his sleeve , and he laughed to himself at how easy it had been to outwit the other birds .
#Text=Higher and higher he mounted , until he was lost to sight , and then folding his wings together , he sank to earth crying shrilly , `` I am king , I am king ! ''
#Text=The eagle tricked by the little bird had not sensed the bird in his feathers and so had not at all expected the bird to come flying out like that .
#Text=The birds back on earth were all up in arms .
#Text=`` You , and not the eagle , our king ? ''
#Text=the birds cried , fuming with anger .
#Text=`` You have done this by breaking every rule in the book , so we will not have you , who are simply tricky and cunning , to reign over us . ''
#Text=The bird without a name then decided to clear the air and said , `` Then let everyone start with a clean slate and perform a new challenging task .
#Text=Then we can decide who should be the real king . ''
#Text=Then the birds gathered together again and decided the case would be resolved by making a new condition , which was that he should be king who could go the deepest into the earth .
#Text=So the little bird who the other birds despised was now back to square one .
#Text=Confident , he remained , however , that if he played his cards right , he could be king .
#Text=How the goose wallowed in the sand , and the duck strove to dig a hole for the new task !
#Text=All the other birds tried to hide themselves in the ground , too , until they were practically blue in the face .
#Text=The nameless little bird that was as bold as brass found a pitch dark mouse 's hole , and creeping in cried , `` I am king , I am king ! ''
#Text=but it was of no avail .
#Text=`` You , our king ? ''
#Text=all the remaining birds who the littlest bird had outwitted cried again , even more angrily than before .
#Text=`` Do you think we would reward your cunning in this way ?
#Text=No , no !
#Text=You shall stay in the earth till you die of hunger ! ''
#Text=So they shut up the little bird in the mouse 's hole that the mouse gave up most unwillingly , and bade the owl watch him carefully night and day .

#Text=Then all the birds went home to bed , for they were very tired , but the owl assigned by the birds to stand guard found his job was lonely and wearisome because he was just sitting alone staring at the mouse 's hole .
#Text=`` I can close one eye and watch with the other , '' he thought .
#Text=So he closed one eye and stared steadfastly with the other , but before he knew it he forgot to keep that one open , and both eyes were fast asleep .
#Text=Then the little bird guarded by the owl peeped out , and when he saw the owl 's two eyes tight shut , he slipped from the hole and flew away .
#Text=He wanted to shout , `` I am king '' so that the owl could hear him as he flew , but thought better of it .
#Text=From this time on , the owl fooled by the little bird has not dared to show himself by day for fear the birds should beat the living daylights out of him .
#Text=He flies about only at nighttime , hating and pursuing not the bird , but the mouse for having made the hole into which the little bird crept .
#Text=And the little bird also keeps out of sight , for he fears that the other birds should punish him for his cunning .
#Text=The rejection by the other birds was a bitter pill to swallow for the nameless bird the owl had let slip away .
#Text=He hides in the hedges , and when he thinks himself quite safe , he sings out , `` I am king , I am king ! ''
#Text=And the other birds in mockery call out , `` Yes , yes , the hedge-king , the hedge-king ! ''
